record.paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: Let G be a graph. A k-list-assignment L assigns k allowable colors to each vertex; a proper L-coloring chooses one allowed color at each vertex and gives adjacent vertices different colors; k proper L-colorings are pairwise disjoint if, at every vertex, all k chosen colors are distinct. Let χℓ(G) be the least k such that every k-list-assignment admits a proper L-coloring, and let χ⋆ℓ(G) be the least k such that every k-list-assignment admits an L-packing of size k. Does there exist a graph G for which χ⋆ℓ(G) is greater than χℓ(G)+1?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1 Is there a graph G for which χ⋆ ℓ(G)> χ ℓ(G) + 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. A $k$-list-assignment on $G$ is a function $L$ that assigns to each vertex $v\in V(G)$ a set $L(v)$ of $k$ allowable colors. A proper $L$-coloring is a function $c$ with $c(v)\in L(v)$ for every $v$ and $c(u)\ne c(v)$ for every edge $uv$. An $L$-packing of size $k$ is a collection of $k$ proper $L$-colorings $c_1,\dots,c_k$ that are pairwise disjoint, meaning that for every vertex $v$ the multiset $\{c_1(v),\dots,c_k(v)\}$ consists of $k$ distinct colors (equivalently, equals $L(v)$).

Define the list chromatic number $\chi_\ell(G)$ to be the smallest integer $k$ such that every $k$-list-assignment $L$ on $G$ admits a proper $L$-coloring. Define the list packing number $\chi^\star_\ell(G)$ to be the smallest integer $k$ such that every $k$-list-assignment $L$ on $G$ admits an $L$-packing of size $k$.

Does there exist a graph $G$ such that
$$\chi^\star_\ell(G) > \chi_\ell(G) + 1\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works on list packing (including results on complete bipartite graphs, bounded-degree graphs, and fractional list packing) discuss the gap between $\chi^\star_\ell$ and $\chi_\ell$ and the List Packing Conjecture, but no example is reported with $\chi^\star_\ell(G) > \chi_\ell(G)+1$. The question of whether such a graph exists appears to remain open as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Packing colourings in complete bipartite graphs and the list packing number
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the list packing number on complete bipartite graphs; raises open questions about the relation between χ⋆ℓ and χℓ.
status_evidence.claim: The relation between list packing number and list chromatic number is an active open area, with the gap question explicitly featured among open problems.

status_evidence.title: List packing number of bounded degree graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes upper bounds on χ⋆ℓ in terms of maximum degree and discusses the List Packing Conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: No graph is known to satisfy χ⋆ℓ(G) > χℓ(G)+1; bounds proceed via degeneracy / Δ(G).

status_evidence.title: Fractional List Packing for Layered Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies fractional list packing variants and confirms fractional analogues of conjectures, leaving the integral gap question open.
status_evidence.claim: The exact gap between χ⋆ℓ and χℓ remains unresolved in the integral setting.
